title: Grade 8 Integrated Science Learning Outcomes: Cells, Matter and Forces (Synthetic Mock Corpus)
subject: Integrated Science

outcomes.topic: Cells and organisation: Observing cells with a light microscope
outcomes.statement: Learners use a light microscope correctly to observe plant cells, calculate total magnification and produce an accurate labelled biological drawing.
successCriteria: Names the eyepiece, objective lens, stage, light source and focus wheels and states the function of each
Focuses a slide on low power before switching to high power
Calculates total magnification by multiplying eyepiece and objective magnifications
Produces a drawing with a title, single clear lines, labels and magnification
evidenceOfLearning: Teacher observation checklist during the practical
Exit ticket with a magnification calculation
outcomes.commonMisconception: Learners often add the lens magnifications instead of multiplying them and start focusing on high power.

outcomes.topic: Cells and organisation: Plant and animal cell structures and functions
outcomes.statement: Learners identify the main structures of plant and animal cells and explain the function of each, including those found only in plant cells.
successCriteria: Labels nucleus, cell membrane, cytoplasm, mitochondria, cell wall, chloroplasts and vacuole correctly
States the function of each structure
Lists structures found only in plant cells
Compares plant and animal cells in a table
evidenceOfLearning: Short written explanations of structure functions
outcomes.commonMisconception: Learners believe plant cells do not have mitochondria or that the cell wall controls what enters the cell.

outcomes.topic: Cells and organisation: Specialised cells and levels of organisation
outcomes.statement: Learners explain how specialised cells are adapted to their functions and order cells, tissues, organs, organ systems and organisms by complexity.
successCriteria: Defines specialised cell, tissue, organ and organ system with examples
Links at least one structural feature to the function of each of three specialised cells
Orders the levels of organisation correctly from cell to organism
evidenceOfLearning: Written explanation of a specialised cell
outcomes.commonMisconception: Learners think all cells have a nucleus or that tissues and organs are the same thing.

outcomes.topic: Matter and the particle model: States of matter and particle arrangement
outcomes.statement: Learners describe and draw the arrangement, spacing and movement of particles in solids, liquids and gases and use the model to explain their properties.
successCriteria: Draws particle diagrams with correct spacing and arrangement for each state
Describes particle movement in each state using terms such as vibrate, slide and move randomly
Uses the model to explain shape, flow and compressibility
outcomes.commonMisconception: Learners believe particles in solids do not move or that there is air between gas particles.

outcomes.topic: Matter and the particle model: Changes of state and particle energy
outcomes.statement: Learners use the particle model to explain melting, freezing, evaporation, condensation and boiling and interpret a heating curve for water.
successCriteria: Names each change of state and describes the particle behaviour involved
Identifies the melting and boiling plateaus on a heating curve
Explains why the temperature stays constant during a change of state
Distinguishes evaporation from boiling
outcomes.commonMisconception: Learners think temperature keeps rising during melting or that boiling and evaporation are the same process.

outcomes.topic: Matter and the particle model: Diffusion and gas pressure
outcomes.statement: Learners explain diffusion and gas pressure using particle motion and describe how temperature affects the rate of diffusion.
successCriteria: Defines diffusion as net movement from higher to lower concentration
Explains why diffusion is faster in hot water than in cold water
Explains gas pressure as collisions of particles with container walls
outcomes.commonMisconception: Learners think diffusion requires stirring or that gas pressure is caused by particles colliding with each other.

outcomes.topic: Forces and motion: Types of forces, newtons and weight
outcomes.statement: Learners classify forces as contact or non-contact, measure forces in newtons and calculate weight using W = m x g with g = 10 N/kg.
successCriteria: Sorts forces into contact and non-contact with examples
Reads a newtonmeter correctly in newtons
Calculates weight from mass with correct units
States that mass does not change with location
outcomes.commonMisconception: Learners treat weight and mass as the same thing.

outcomes.topic: Forces and motion: Balanced and unbalanced forces
outcomes.statement: Learners draw force diagrams, determine resultant force and explain how balanced and unbalanced forces affect motion.
successCriteria: Draws force arrows with correct direction and relative size
Calculates the resultant of two forces in one dimension
Explains that balanced forces mean constant speed or rest
Explains that unbalanced forces change speed or direction
outcomes.commonMisconception: Learners believe a force is required to keep an object moving at constant speed.

outcomes.topic: Forces and motion: Speed, distance and time
outcomes.statement: Learners calculate speed from distance and time and interpret distance-time graphs.
successCriteria: Calculates speed using speed = distance / time with correct units
Plots a distance-time graph from data
Identifies stationary and faster motion from graph shape
Converts between m/s and km/h
outcomes.commonMisconception: Learners think a horizontal line on a distance-time graph means constant speed.
